problems.statement: The Dean's presented claim that central IT is generally unresponsive to Arts is mostly not supported: outside two specific pockets, Arts remote tickets are resolved on par with other faculties.

The main driver of Arts' slow resolution is SlotBook tickets, which RR-17 routes to an unstaffed P4 best-effort queue with no resolution target (median 21 days, 17 of them waiting for first action, 1.6 days hands-on); removing them closes about 70% of the gap.

A second, separate driver is thin on-site cover at the Lindqvist satellite campus (technician Tuesdays and Thursdays only), which delays on-site hardware tickets for Arts and Education alike (6.4-6.5 days vs 1.8); wait is for technician arrival, not repair.

The routing change was governed and communicated poorly: the change record has no external-notification step, the auto-acknowledgement for SlotBook tickets gives no hint of best-effort status, and no handover note existed, so requesters and Arts management have been unable to see or plan around the P4 status.

Whether the ITS Director actually told the former Arts Operations Manager about RR-17 on 2025-08-12 cannot be determined; the Dean's claim that nobody told Arts and the Director's claim that Arts knew are both unverified and not needed to decide what to do.

ITS's account that Arts over-raises trivial and duplicate tickets is largely not supported: duplicate rate (4.1% vs 3.9%) and how-to share are comparable, and the excess ticket volume comes from SlotBook plus the on-site hardware share.

The unsupported, undocumented SlotBook (PHP 5.6, no agreement, no owner, unmanaged server) is an underlying structural problem that ITS and Arts have both left unresolved, with no fit assessment or migration scoped for the CampusBook alternative that the Department says cannot handle repeating multi-section patterns.
The September 2025 SlotBook ticket spike and login problems were caused by the single sign-on migration.
Widespread dissatisfaction in Arts is real but is mostly attributable to SlotBook and timetabling rather than ITS across the board; the survey is low-response and cannot be taken as representative.
Anecdotes of generally slow ITS service (e.g. Philosophy email migration) reflect time awaiting the requester rather than ITS delay.
Service desk capacity is a general cause of Arts delays.

actions.action: Do not endorse transferring 2 FTE to an Arts-run desk; it would not fix the unsupported SlotBook or Lindqvist on-site cover, and would remove roughly 10% of a desk running at 94% utilisation.
actions.rationale: The evidence shows the delay is concentrated in SlotBook routing and on-site cover, which a small Arts desk with the same unsupported app and no server access would not resolve.

actions.action: Do not adopt ITS's proposal to put all Arts tickets on the best-effort track.
actions.rationale: Arts non-SlotBook remote tickets perform in line with the rest of the university, so this would penalise staff for a problem confined to one application.

actions.action: Have ITS immediately rewrite ACK-P4 to state best-effort status and expected timeframe, add an external-notification step to routing-rule changes, and formally brief the current Arts Faculty Operations Manager and Dean on RR-17.
actions.rationale: Cheap, within ITS control, and removes the invisibility that turned a policy decision into a perception of silence.

actions.action: Agree an explicit interim service level for SlotBook-related room clashes (named triage owner, target time, escalation) while the application's future is decided, rather than leaving them in a 0.4 FTE no-target queue.
actions.rationale: SlotBook drives most of the gap and timetabling failures hit teaching directly.

actions.action: Commission a joint ITS-Arts requirements-fit assessment of CampusBook against SlotBook (including repeating multi-section patterns) and a risk review of the PHP 5.6 server before any January 2027 migration deadline is fixed.
actions.rationale: No fit assessment exists and the Department says CampusBook cannot do its patterns, so forcing a cutover risks harming timetabling.

actions.action: Review on-site technician cover for the Lindqvist campus (extra days, scheduled slots, or remote-hands for simple hardware).
actions.rationale: Technician arrival wait (4.7 vs 0.6 days) explains slow hardware resolution for both Arts and Education, and repair time is short.

actions.action: Present the Dean's Provost proposal as a documented set of findings that set out the two actual drivers rather than a claim of general unresponsiveness.
actions.rationale: Gives the Dean an evidence-based case while correcting the framing.

actions.action: Investigate whether the SSO migration is behind SlotBook login problems once ITS can access server logs.
actions.rationale: Causal link is unconfirmed and ITS has no log access.

actions.action: Attribute blame for the notification dispute to either the Director or the former manager.
actions.rationale: No records or testimony can settle it, and the governance gap is evident either way.

A CampusBook versus SlotBook requirements-fit and migration-cost assessment, including repeating multi-section timetable patterns and the 1,900 teaching sections
Lindqvist on-site demand profile and cost of extra technician days or remote-hands cover, plus repeat-contact and timetable-clash impact data for SlotBook tickets
output.summary: Arts' slower service is real but narrow, not general unresponsiveness. About 70% of the gap comes from SlotBook tickets, which routing rule RR-17 sends to an unstaffed best-effort queue (median 21 days). Most of the rest is on-site hardware delay from part-week technician cover at Lindqvist, which also affects Education. Other Arts tickets perform in line with the university. ITS's duplicate/trivial-ticket claim is not supported. Nobody can show whether Arts was told, but the governance gap (no notification step, uninformative acknowledgement, no handover) is clear. Reject the Arts-run desk and the all-Arts best-effort proposals. Fix communication, interim SlotBook triage, a migration fit assessment, and Lindqvist cover.
